reason: Moses is portrayed throughout this passage as the primary representative and leader of the Israelites in negotiations with Pharaoh. He directly addresses Pharaoh multiple times, relays God's commands to him, and performs miracles as demonstrations of divine authority to compel Pharaoh to release his people (עַמִּי - 'my people'). Moses acts as the spokeswoman/negotiator for the entire Israelite nation, seeking their liberation and establishment as a free people. He operates with clear authority over the Israelites and acts decisively on their behalf, establishing him as a national leader.
